text:
ops-bot: [INCIDENT] PagerDuty alert PD-48321 -> elevated 5xx rate on /v1/generate. Please acknowledge if oncall. urgency=high :rotating_light:

pagerduty-bot: PD-48321 acknowledged by maria at 2026-03-14T21:09:05Z :thumbsup:

maria: seeing a sharp spike of 504/502 from ingress-gw-az1 around 21:07-21:12 UTC. Error payloads show upstream timeout + retries. Sample log line:
```
[2026-03-14T21:08:02Z] req=6f3a29ef gateway=ingress-gw-az1 upstream=egress-proxy backend_status=timeout retry_count=3 latency_ms=1200 path=/v1/generate user=acct-42
```

maria: correlating a handful of req ids now -> looks like ingress retried twice, which amplified load to egress-proxy. Noting correlation ids: 6f3a29ef, 6f3a2b12, 6f3a2d9a.

ashley: on it. pulling traces for those req ids via trace-service. running: `tracectl get --ids 6f3a29ef,6f3a2b12 -o timeline` :eyes:

trace-bot: trace results linked -> https://traces.internal.redwood/trace/6f3a29ef  (shortpayload, shows repeated outbound calls to egress-proxy)

ashley: confirmed repeated outbound retries in timeline. egress-proxy returned 504s after ~1.2s, ingress retried 2x causing fanout. hypothesis A: retries amplifying transient egress slowness.

samir: customer impact estimate from metrics: 2.1% error rate in us-east-1, peak qps for /v1/generate down 8%. Large customers (acct-142, acct-88) reporting degraded UX. I'm sending an incident email to CS and sales now.

maria: immediate mitigation plan: 1) disable client-side retries for /v1/generate at ingress (set max_retries=0) 2) enable route fallback to cheaper model-variant temporarily 3) open traffic to other regions for failover. I'll push the ingress config change now.

drew: +1. recommend also reducing ingress concurrency for the route to prevent head-of-line. I'll apply a temporary rate-limit (burst=50, rate=100r/s) and remove retries.

maria: applied config change at 21:15 UTC: `ingress-config set /v1/generate retries=0 concurrency=100` -> observed drop in retry amplification within ~90s. Metrics: 504 rate decreased from 4.8% -> 1.2% by 21:17.

ashley: checking egress-proxy pools. Initial look: egress-proxy cpu ~92% on az1, thread_pool exhausted, connection queue growing. sample egress log:
```
[2026-03-14T21:06:58Z] egress-proxy|pool=main threads=64 busy=64 queue=312 conn_wait_ms=240 backend_call=runtime-01 status=timeout
```

ashley: hypothesis B: egress-proxy thread pool exhaustion due to bursty retries plus one backend model runtime latency spike. Investigating backend runtime metrics now.

maria: can we confirm if any model-hosting autoscaler failed to scale? Drew, can you check model-hosting-01 autoscaler events?

drew: checking: autoscaler logs show a scale-up but with a delay ~30s due to node provisioning in az1. There was a small cluster autoscaling jitter around 21:05-21:09.

samir: timeline so far: 21:05 small lat spike on runtime -> 21:06 ingress retries start amplifying -> 21:07 egress-proxy queue grows -> 21:09 PagerDuty fires -> 21:15 retries disabled -> 21:17 error rate improving. I'll put this into a timeline doc.

maria: mitigation checklist next: - keep retries disabled for 1 hour - increase egress-proxy thread pool in az1 (+20) - add a short-term header to route to force fallback variant for large requests (hash-based) - collect all correlation ids for RCA.

ashley: increasing egress-proxy pool now (patch rolling restart). command: `kubectl -n prod scale deployment/egress-proxy --replicas=6` -> rolling restart started at 21:20.

trace-bot: log bundle for 21:00-21:30 uploaded -> https://logs.redwood/s3/incident/PD-48321-bundle.tar.gz (contains ingress, egress, runtime traces + correlation index)

maria: good. @oncall-night you'll take the next 30m watch and own the incident until the formal handoff. Please annotate the timeline with any regressions.

oncall-night: taking this handoff at 21:30 UTC. I'll keep monitoring. :hand:

drew: quick note on mitigations: re-enable retries only after we validate egress latency stable for 15m and autoscaler steady. Also add a safety cap on retry amplification: ingress should not fanout to more than 2 upstream calls within 2s.

samir: customer comms: Sent initial status to impacted customers, flagged postmortem likely. Need to collect exact request ids for support. Support request template: `req=6f3a29ef time=21:08 region=us-east-1 error=504`

maria: collecting RCA artifacts: - trace links (trace-bot) - log bundle (trace-bot) - autoscaler events (drew) - egress-proxy metrics (ashley) - ingress config diff (maria). I'll create the RCA draft in docs/incidents/PD-48321 after we stabilize.

ashley: current status at 21:27 UTC: error rate now ~0.9%, ingress latency back to baseline for most traffic. egress-proxy CPU dropped after scale-up. keeping changes for 1 hour.

maria: note for post-incident action items (IA): 1) add smarter retry budget (circuit-breaker) 2) autoscaler tuning/fast path for model-hosting scale-up 3) better observability around request fanout and amplification 4) add synthetic checks for model runtime latency in each AZ.

drew: cc:@infra, we should consider warm pool for runtime nodes in heavy regions to avoid scale-up delay.

samir: adding customer-impact numbers to the incident doc now and tagging CS.

maria: final note before handoff: collect any additional req ids that hit 504 between 21:05-21:16 and drop them into this thread. We'll use them in the RCA for example timelines.

ashley: posting a few more req ids observed: 6f3a2f01, 6f3a3018, 6f3a33b7.

oncall-night: ack. I'll keep monitoring and will escalate if we see regression. Preparing a short comms update at 22:00 UTC.

ops-bot: incident PD-48321 status -> mitigated (partial). Owner: maria. Next update scheduled at 22:00 UTC. :white_check_mark:

maria: thanks everyone. I'll own the RCA write-up and tag you all for review.

(END OF THREAD)
